사.forms: Sino-Korean · dates, money, minutes, phone numbers, floors (사 층, 사월)
사.x: Lots of flowers bloom in April.
사.e: Considered unlucky, like 13 in the US.
사.t: The number 4 (사) sounds like the word for 'death', so some elevators show F instead of 4 for the fourth floor.

이야기하다.m: to talk, to tell, to chat
이야기하다.x: I talked with my friend for a long time at a café.
이야기하다.e: 이야기 (story, talk) + 하다 (do); often shortened to 얘기하다 in speech.

들리다.m: to be heard, to be audible
들리다.x: I can hear music from outside.
들리다.e: Passive of 듣다 (hear); 잘 들려요? = Can you hear me?
들리다.t: The sound takes 이/가: 소리가 들려요. On the phone: 잘 안 들려요 'I can't hear you well.'

그러나.forms: written/formal; in speech use 하지만 or 그런데
그러나.ex: 그 식당은 비쌉니다. 그러나 음식이 맛있습니다.
그러나.x: That restaurant is expensive. However, the food is delicious.
그러나.e: From 그러하다 (to be so) + -나 (but). More written than 하지만 or 그런데.
그러나.t: Mostly used in writing and formal speeches.

하지만.forms: starts a sentence: A. 하지만 B. · within a sentence use -지만
하지만.x: Korean is difficult. But it's fun.

그치다.m: to stop (of rain, snow or crying)
그치다.x: When the rain stops, let's go for a walk together.
그치다.e: Used for things that stop on their own.
그치다.t: 그치다 is for rain, snow or crying; for cars or machines that stop, use 멈추다.

데우다.m: to heat up, to warm up (food or drinks)
데우다.ex: 자기 전에 전자레인지에 우유를 데워서 마셨어요.
데우다.x: Before bed, I warmed some milk in the microwave and drank it.
데우다.e: Used for reheating: 다시 데우다 'to reheat'. The opposite is letting food 식다 'cool'.

이따가.m: a little later (today), in a while
이따가.ex: 이따가 회사 앞에서 점심 같이 먹어요.
이따가.x: Let's have lunch together in front of the office a little later.
이따가.t: Don't confuse it with 있다가 'stay and then'; 이따가 means 'later today'.

저기요.x: Excuse me, could we get some water here?
저기요.e: 저기 'over there' + 요 for politeness — literally 'over there!'
저기요.t: In restaurants, calling staff with 저기요 or 여기요 is polite and completely normal.

연구원.x: My older brother works as a researcher at a company lab.
연구원.e: Literally 'research member'. A homonym (different hanja) means 'research institute'.

깊이.x: This lake is about ten meters deep.
깊이.e: From 깊다 'deep' + -이; as an adverb, 깊이 also means 'deeply'.
깊이.t: Pronounced [기피]; the same -이 pattern makes 높이 'height' and 길이 'length.'

스스로.m: by oneself, on one's own; oneself
스스로.ex: 우리 아이는 이제 스스로 옷을 입어요.
스스로.x: My child now gets dressed on her own.
스스로.t: 스스로 stresses doing it without help; 혼자 stresses being alone.

견디다.m: to endure, to bear, to stand, to withstand
견디다.x: It's so hard to endure the summer heat.
견디다.t: 참다 is holding back a feeling or urge; 견디다 is lasting through a hard situation over time.

황당하다.ex: 택시 기사님이 길을 몰라서 정말 황당했어요.
황당하다.x: The taxi driver didn't know the way, so I was totally dumbfounded.
황당하다.e: Originally described wild, groundless talk; now used for 'What on earth?!' moments.
황당하다.t: Don't mix it up with 당황하다: 황당하다 means the situation is absurd, 당황하다 means you're flustered.

저절로.x: The wind blew and the door opened by itself.
저절로.e: Short form 절로 means the same; think 저 'oneself' — it happens on its own.

미치다.m: to affect, have (an effect); to reach
미치다.x: Smartphones have a big influence on children.
미치다.e: Homonym warning: another 미치다 means 'to go crazy'.
미치다.t: Learn it as the collocation 영향을 미치다 'to have an influence on'.

재테크.ex: 요즘은 젊은 사람들도 재테크에 관심이 많아요.
재테크.x: These days even young people are very interested in growing their money.
재테크.e: Blend of 재 'wealth' + 테크 from English 'tech(nology)': the technique of growing money.
재테크.t: 재테크 covers savings, stocks and real estate; English has no single word for it.

방역.ex: 정부는 전염병을 막기 위해 방역을 강화했습니다.
방역.x: The government tightened disease-control measures to stop the epidemic.

흥행.ex: 그 영화는 관객 천만 명을 넘으며 크게 흥행했어요.
흥행.x: That movie was a huge hit, drawing more than ten million viewers.
흥행.e: Originally 'running a show for profit'; now mostly means being a hit.
흥행.t: 흥행에 성공하다/실패하다 means to be a box-office hit or flop.

거리감.m: sense of distance; emotional distance, feeling of detachment
거리감.ex: 그 친구와 오랜만에 만나니 거리감이 느껴졌어요.
거리감.x: Meeting that friend after a long time, I felt some distance between us.
거리감.e: Literally 'feeling of distance'; -감 = feeling: 책임감, 안정감.

속성.ex: 물은 높은 곳에서 낮은 곳으로 흐르는 속성이 있어요.
속성.x: Water has the property of flowing from high places to low places.
속성.e: Literally 'belonging nature': the qualities that come with a thing.
속성.t: Pronounced [속썽]; a homonym 속성 means 'crash course', as in ads for 속성 과외.

양면성.ex: 인터넷은 편리함과 위험이라는 양면성을 가지고 있어요.
양면성.x: The internet has two sides: convenience and danger.
양면성.e: Literally 'the quality of having two sides'.

시부모.x: I go to see my parents-in-law every weekend.
시부모.e: 시- marks the husband's side: 시아버지, 시어머니, 시댁.
시부모.t: In polite speech, almost always add 님: 시부모님.

농성.ex: 노동자들이 회사 앞에서 농성을 벌이고 있어요.
농성.x: Workers are staging a sit-in in front of the company.
농성.e: Originally 'shutting oneself inside a castle' under siege; now a sit-in protest.
농성.t: Collocations: 농성을 벌이다, 단식 농성 (hunger-strike sit-in), 천막 농성 (tent sit-in).

시민권.ex: 그는 미국에서 태어나서 미국 시민권을 가지고 있어요.
시민권.x: He was born in America, so he has U.S. citizenship.
시민권.e: Literally 'citizen's right'. -권 = right: 영주권, 투표권, 인권.
시민권.t: Pronounced [시민꿘]; 시민권을 따다 is the casual way to say 'get citizenship'.

저소득층.x: The government is providing living expenses to low-income households.

어우러지다.m: to blend in, to go well together, to harmonize; to mingle (of people)
어우러지다.x: It's a city where tradition and modernity blend well.
어우러지다.e: Related to 어울리다 'to suit, to go together' — both describe things fitting together.
어우러지다.t: Positive nuance: 뒤섞이다 is a jumble, while 어우러지다 is a pleasing harmony.

모질다.ex: 그렇게 모진 말을 하면 친구가 상처받아요.
모질다.x: If you say such harsh words, your friend will get hurt.
모질다.t: 모질게 마음먹다 'to steel yourself' shows the positive, tough side of the word.

합당하다.x: You should get a reward that matches your effort.
합당하다.t: Pattern: N에 합당하다 'to be fitting for N'.

아련히.x: Memories of my childhood come back to me faintly.
아련히.e: Adverb of 아련하다; carries a soft, wistful, nostalgic feeling.

도마 위에 오르다.forms: 도마 위에 올라요 · 도마 위에 올랐어요 (르 irregular)
도마 위에 오르다.m: to come under fire; to become the target of criticism
도마 위에 오르다.ex: 그 정책이 국회에서 도마 위에 올랐습니다.
도마 위에 오르다.x: The policy came under fire in the National Assembly.
도마 위에 오르다.e: Literally 'to be put on the cutting board,' like food about to be cut.
도마 위에 오르다.t: Often shortened to 도마에 오르다; frequent in news about officials and policies.
rel: to become the subject of gossip

베일에 싸이다.forms: 베일에 싸여 있어요 · 베일에 싸였어요 · 베일에 싸인 + noun
베일에 싸이다.m: to be shrouded in mystery; to be kept under wraps
베일에 싸이다.ex: 새 휴대폰의 디자인은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
베일에 싸이다.x: The new phone's design is still under wraps.
베일에 싸이다.e: From English 'veil'; literally 'to be wrapped in a veil.'

갈림길.m: fork in the road, crossroads; turning point
갈림길.x: At a crossroads in my life, I chose to study abroad.
갈림길.e: 갈리다 'to split' + 길 'road' — where the road splits.
갈림길.t: Pronounced [갈림낄] — the ㄱ in 길 is tensed in this compound.

허무감.x: When the exam was over, a sudden feeling of emptiness washed over me.
허무감.t: Typical verbs: 허무감이 들다 or 허무감을 느끼다 (to feel empty).

송전탑.ex: 마을 주민들이 새 송전탑 건설에 반대하고 있어요.
송전탑.x: Village residents are opposing the construction of a new transmission tower.

이원론.ex: 데카르트의 이원론은 정신과 육체를 분리해서 봅니다.
이원론.x: Descartes' dualism views the mind and the body as separate.
이원론.t: Standard pronunciation is [이원논], not [이월론], a textbook exception.

사이비.ex: 사이비 종교에 빠져 재산을 모두 잃은 사람도 있어요.
사이비.x: Some people have lost everything after getting caught up in a cult.
사이비.e: Literally 'looks like it, and yet isn't'; from a saying in Mencius.
사이비.t: Works like a prefix: 사이비 종교 (cult), 사이비 의사 (quack doctor), 사이비 기자 (fake journalist).

인지부조화.ex: 담배가 해롭다는 걸 알면서 피우는 것은 인지부조화예요.
인지부조화.x: Smoking while knowing it's harmful is cognitive dissonance.

골다공증.ex: 골다공증을 예방하려면 칼슘을 충분히 먹어야 해요.
골다공증.x: To prevent osteoporosis, you should get enough calcium.
골다공증.t: Pronounced [골다공쯩]; -증 means 'symptom or condition' and appears in many illness names.

역작.m: work of great effort, labor of love, masterpiece
역작.ex: 이 소설은 작가가 10년 동안 공들여 쓴 역작입니다.
역작.x: This novel is a labor of love the author spent ten years writing.
역작.e: Literally 'strength work' — made with tremendous effort.
역작.t: Pronounced [역짝]; often paired with 심혈을 기울인 'poured heart and soul into.'

흐드러지다.x: Spring has come, and the cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

무던히.forms: 무던히 + verb: 무던히 애쓰다 · 무던히 참다
무던히.m: patiently, steadily; quite a lot, considerably
무던히.ex: 그는 그 일을 끝내려고 무던히 애를 썼어요.
무던히.x: He tried really hard to finish that work.

명목.ex: 회사는 비용 절감을 명목으로 직원을 줄였습니다.
명목.x: The company cut staff under the pretext of reducing costs.
명목.e: Literally 'name and item': what something is called, not what it really is.
명목.t: The pattern ~을/를 명목으로 means 'under the name or pretext of ~'.

육종.ex: 육종은 뼈나 근육에 생기는 드문 암입니다.
육종.x: Sarcoma is a rare cancer that develops in bone or muscle.
육종.e: Literally 'flesh swelling': a tumor of the body's connective tissue.
육종.t: Homonym: 육종 (育種) also means 'breeding' of plants or animals; pronounced [육쫑].
